answer: If I could live anywhere, I would choose a quiet coastal town, somewhere that balances natural beauty with a sense of community. I am thinking of somewhere like the area around Inani, south of Cox's Bazar, where green hills come right down towards the beach. I have always been drawn to the sea, so waking up to the sound of waves would be genuinely [[idyllic]] for me. I imagine a place that is peaceful but not isolated, with friendly neighbours, a small market and a slower pace of life. What appeals to me most is the idea of escaping the relentless [[hustle and bustle]] of big cities like Dhaka, which I find exhausting whenever I visit. I would love to spend my mornings walking along the shore and my evenings watching the sunset. During the day I could work remotely, advising students online, which is becoming quite possible in my field. At the weekends I might learn to fish or simply read on a balcony facing the sea. I think such an environment would be far more [[conducive]] to a healthy, balanced lifestyle. Of course, I would still want decent amenities nearby, such as a hospital and good internet, so it would need to be reasonably [[well connected]], and close enough for my parents to visit. Honestly, the thought of such a calm, [[wholesome]] existence is very appealing. Perhaps one day, when my career allows it, I will make that dream a reality.

followUps.q: Do you think you will actually live there one day?
followUps.answer: Perhaps, though probably not for many years. For now my family and my career are here, but it is a dream I keep at the back of my mind, maybe for later in life.

followUps.q: Would your family be happy if you moved away?
followUps.answer: My parents would probably worry at first, as they like having us close. But if I were within a day's journey and visited often, I think they would gradually come round to the idea.

note: Gave a real example (Inani, near Cox's Bazar); 'hustle of the city' reframed as big cities like Dhaka since he lives in a town; added remote work and family ties; 'hustle' widened to 'hustle and bustle', added 'well connected'.
